nodes.description: ARH knockout mouse used to test, in an intact liver, the same recombinant ARH domain constructs characterized in polarized WIF-B hepatocytes. The in-vivo studies confirmed that the cell-culture domain requirements for LDL receptor clustering and internalization hold in the hepatocyte compartment of a whole animal - the in-vivo confirmation of the entry's central mechanism.

Homozygous or compound-heterozygous loss-of-function variants in LDLRAP1 at 1p35, the causal lesion of ARH. The gene encodes the LDL receptor adaptor protein (ARH). Causative alleles are heterogeneous but are all predicted to be loss-of-function, and the Sardinian founder alleles ARH1 and ARH2 account for most reported cases.

evidence.snippet: Here we map the ARH locus to an approximately 1-centimorgan interval on chromosome 1p35 and identify six mutations in a gene encoding a putative adaptor protein (ARH).

genetic_context.description: Biallelic loss-of-function is required; heterozygotes are unaffected. Recorded on the genetic context because the claim is about the consequence of the alleles. Compound-heterozygous genotypes are also seen; HOMOZYGOUS is used here for the common founder-allele case.

nodes.description: In hepatocytes, LDL-bound receptor fails to cluster into clathrin-coated pits and is not internalized. The defect is cell-type specific: LDL receptor endocytosis is impaired in the liver but not in fibroblasts, where the redundant adaptor Dab2 substitutes for ARH. This tissue specificity is the signature of ARH and explains why the systemic LDL clearance defect is driven by the hepatic compartment even though the receptor is normal everywhere.

nodes.description: The defining biochemical phenotype: markedly and persistently elevated plasma LDL cholesterol, at levels comparable to receptor-defective homozygous FH. Because conventional receptor-dependent therapies act by increasing LDL receptor number, and the ARH receptor cannot internalize LDL regardless of number, LDL-C in ARH patients typically remains far from target on statin, ezetimibe, and apheresis therapy.

nodes.description: Extracorporeal physical removal of circulating apoB-containing lipoproteins, used in severe ARH (as in homozygous FH) when pharmacotherapy leaves LDL-C far above target and there is established cardiovascular disease. Its LDL lowering is mechanism-independent - it removes LDL directly from plasma.

evidence.snippet: LDL apheresis is also used occasionally if there is evidence of established CAD.

nodes.description: Microsomal triglyceride transfer protein (MTP) inhibitor. It reduces hepatic VLDL secretion and therefore LDL production by an LDL-receptor-independent mechanism, which is why it retains efficacy in ARH despite the receptor internalization defect. In a subanalysis of nine ARH patients in the Pan-European Lomitapide Study, adding lomitapide to background statin plus ezetimibe achieved a median on-treatment LDL-C of 101.7 mg/dL (a 60.4% reduction from baseline).

evidence.reference_title: Efficacy of Long-Term Treatment of Autosomal Recessive Hypercholesterolemia With Lomitapide: A Subanalysis of the Pan-European Lomitapide Study.
evidence.snippet: The addition of lomitapide (mean dose, 10 mg) resulted in the achievement of a median on-treatment LDL-C of 101.7 mg/dL (IQR, 71.3-138.3; 60.4% reduction from baseline)

evidence.reference_title: Autosomal recessive hypercholesterolemia: update for 2020.

nodes.description: The ARH protein normally uses its PTB domain to bind the FDNPVY / NPxY motif in the LDL receptor cytoplasmic tail, and separate clathrin-box and AP-2 binding regions to tether the bound receptor to clathrin and AP-2. When ARH is lost, this molecular bridge is absent. Crucially the LDL receptor protein itself is intact and normally expressed - the defect is in the cytosolic adaptor, not the receptor.

evidence.snippet: The phosphotyrosine binding domain of ARH plus either the clathrin box or the AP-2 binding region were required for both clustering and internalization of the LDLR.

nodes.description: Monoclonal antibodies against PCSK9 (e.g., alirocumab, evolocumab) raise LDL receptor surface abundance. Their benefit in ARH is disputed and at best partial, because their action depends on residual LDL receptor functionality and, in ARH lymphocytes, surface LDL receptor is already higher than normal and PCSK9's effect on it is blunted. They may lower LDL-C in some ARH patients on top of statin therapy.

nodes.description: Accelerated atherosclerosis of the coronary arteries and proximal aorta, plus aortic valve stenosis, developing decades earlier than in the general population. ARH is considered a phenocopy of homozygous FH for cardiovascular risk, and the risk of aortic valve stenosis is a recognized feature. The distal LDL-to-plaque cascade is not re-derived here; this node conforms to the shared atherogenesis module's clinical end state, into which the lifelong LDL-C elevation feeds.

nodes.description: First-line conventional therapy, but ARH is relatively resistant to it: LDL-C remains far from target despite intensive statin-plus-ezetimibe treatment. Mechanistically, a statin lowers hepatic cholesterol and induces more LDL receptor, but in ARH the additional receptor still cannot internalize LDL without the adaptor; ezetimibe blocks intestinal cholesterol absorption (NPC1L1) and so acts by an ARH-independent route, which is why the combination still lowers LDL-C partially.
